dedupe_keys.name: indoorcontact agent based simulation of indoor contact between pedestrians

description: indoorContact is a Python agent-based model that simulates how people move and come into contact in indoor spaces, to observe individual patterns of spatiotemporal contact shaped by interactions between agents and indoor structures. It was written by Moongi Choi; the ABM version was archived on Zenodo on 13 March 2024 and is installable from PyPI as indoorContact (version 0.1.0). A simulation creates an indoor space of given width and height with optional randomly placed 1-metre obstacles, or imports a grid layout, sets entrances where agents enter and leave, and initialises parameters; agents head straight for destinations and otherwise choose among eight directions to get round obstacles, and contact time between agents is measured from their proximity. Coverage: generic indoor spaces defined by the user. Access: GitHub repository (ABM branch), PyPI and Zenodo. Licence: Zenodo lists CC BY 4.0 for the archive; free. Caveats: a simple research model with one release. Simulation uses: infection exposure and crowding in buildings such as shops, offices and stations, and testing layout or occupancy limits. Related records: JuPedSim and the flood-pedestrian simulator.
